title: The medicine of immortality
hookLine: Ignatius calls the Eucharist the medicine of immortality and stresses unity with the bishop

cards: A bathroom cabinet is a small pharmacy: something for headaches, something for a cough, a half-finished prescription. Medicine is an ordinary thing to keep in a house.
It's also an admission: bodies break, and everyone would like to put off the end a little longer.
Ignatius, still on his road to Rome, reaches for exactly that ordinary word when he writes about the bread Christians share.

teach.b: Writing to the Christians of Ephesus, Ignatius asks them to gather in one faith around their bishop and priests, breaking one bread, which he calls "the medicine of immortality": an antidote, he adds, so that we should not die but live forever in Jesus Christ.
In Greek, pharmakon athanasias. The cure for death, handed out at a table. Second, where the picture comes from.

In John's Gospel Jesus says, in the Douay-Rheims: "I am the living bread which came down from heaven." Whoever eats this bread, he goes on, will live forever. Ignatius gives that hope a household name: medicine.
Third, why the bishop comes into it. For Ignatius, the cure works in a body that holds together.

teach.h: ONE CUP, ONE ALTAR, ONE BISHOP.
teach.b: To Philadelphia he writes: take care to keep one Eucharist, for there is one flesh of our Lord, one cup, one altar, as there is one bishop.
To Smyrna he says the Eucharist should be the one celebrated with the bishop, or someone he appoints. Earlier in the letter to Ephesus, he calls Christ the one physician. Fourth, how it's read today.
Catholics, and Orthodox Christians too, read Ignatius as an early witness to what they believe: that the Eucharist is truly the body and blood of Christ, celebrated in communion with the bishop.
In the letter to Smyrna he mentions people who stayed away from the Eucharist because they did not confess it to be the flesh of Christ.
Some Protestant readers treasure his letters while reading these lines in their own way.
At every Catholic Mass, the local bishop is still named aloud in the Eucharistic Prayer, right in the middle of the bread and the cup.
One bread, one bishop, said at once.

how: At every Catholic Mass the local bishop is named in the Eucharistic Prayer, and Catholics receive Communion as the body and blood of Christ, in communion with their bishop and the pope.

games.why: Ignatius says there is one flesh of the Lord, one cup, one altar and one bishop, so keep one Eucharist.

practice: If you're Catholic and know your bishop's name, hold it in mind, or listen for it in the Eucharistic Prayer next time you're at Mass; on another path, think of whoever holds your community together, a pastor, a principal, a parent.
Picture them on a hard day, with everyone's complaints on their desk. If you pray, ask wisdom and strength for them; if you don't, wish them well, plainly.

wordCard.voice: pharmakon athanasias. Ignatius's Greek name for the Eucharist: the medicine of immortality, the one bread that keeps a church whole. Today's word.
